land.text: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya that remained to the Uzbeks after Shaybani's death

predecessors.note: The Khanate of Bukhara page dates the khanate from 1501 ('Muhammad Shaybani conquers Bukhara from Timurid Empire: 1501'); Cliopatria has Shaybanids 1497-1511 and Bukhara from 1516, so the Uzbek state is split at 1511/1512 here.

land.text: the whole khanate: 'In 1785, his descendant, Shah Murad, formalized the family's dynastic rule' as emirs

successors.note: The Emirate page says it 'was officially created in 1785'; Cliopatria's Emirate row starts 1788, so 1786-1787 are covered by this dossier's last shape (extended) and the Emirate dossier should start in 1785.

capitals.name: Bukhara
capitals.note: The infobox says 'Capital: None (1501-1562); Bukhara (from 1562)': the early khanate was governed from Balkh, Bukhara, Samarkand and Tashkent, and the page itself gives a second date (Bukhara capital under Abdullah, 1581-1598). Bukhara is drawn throughout for want of a fixed seat before 1562.

rulers.name: Ubaydullah Khan
rulers.note: Khan of Bukhara 1534-1539 (born 1487, died 1539); he held Bukhara from 1510-1512 as governor, before he was supreme khan.

rulers.name: Abdullah Khan II
rulers.note: 'the last uncontested Shaybanid Khan of Bukhara from 1583 until his death'; the Khanate page also gives 1557, 1561 and 1581 for his rise.

rulers.name: Baqi Muhammad Khan
rulers.note: First Janid (Ashtarkhanid) khan; defeated Pir Muhammad II in 1599.

rulers.name: Abd al-Aziz Khan
rulers.note: The Janid page gives 1680 in the list and 1681 in the table.

rulers.name: Abu al-Fayz Khan
rulers.note: Killed in 1747 by the ataliq Muhammad Rahim (Emirate of Bukhara page).

rulers.name: Muhammad Abd al-Mumin
rulers.title: puppet khan under the Manghit ataliq

rulers.name: Muhammad Ubaidullah II
rulers.title: puppet khan under the Manghit ataliq

rulers.name: Abu'l Ghazi
rulers.title: puppet khan under the ataliqs
rulers.note: The Janid page lists an unnamed ruler for 1753-1758.

correction.text: Transoxiana and the Balkh country: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, which the Uzbeks held from 1512 (Ghazdewan)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1512-1515, the years Cliopatria leaves empty (Shaybanids end 1511, Bukhara starts 1516; its Timurid row draws Babur's 1512-1515 shape over Transoxiana). After Shaybani's death Bukhara went to Ubaidullah, who defended it against Babur and the Safavids in 1511-1512, and Babur's defeat at Ghazdewan 'finally secured the Uzbeks' possession of the land between Amu Darya and Syr Darya'. The Cliopatria 1521 shape (Transoxiana, Balkh, Kunduz, no Syr Darya towns) is used.

correction.text: the 1521 shape: Transoxiana and Balkh without the Syr Darya towns Tashkent, Turkestan and Sayram, which the Kazakh Khanate held or contested

keyframe_review.note: 712,247 km2 for 1516-1520: the shape reaches Tashkent, Turkestan, Shymkent and the Syr Darya steppe to 46.6 N. The Kazakh Khanate page has Kasym Khan's southern border run 'to the right bank of the Syr Darya, including Tashkent, Turkestan, and Sayram' by the end of his reign (about 1521), and 'in the winter of 1516-1517, Uzbek forces approached Tashkent but failed to capture it'. Cliopatria's own Kazakh row takes those towns in 1521. The Syr Darya towns are therefore removed for 1516-1520 and drawn as contested (ledger). No infobox area to compare (the page gives only a 1902 population of 2,000,000).

384,353 km2 for 1521-1525: Transoxiana, Fergana and Khujand, Balkh and Kunduz, without the Syr Darya towns. Consistent with the Kazakh Khanate page (Kasym's border on the Syr Darya by 1521) and with the Khanate of Bukhara page (Samarkand, Bukhara and Andijan Uzbek).

correction.text: Transoxiana and Balkh as in 1521; Khorasan (Herat, Mashhad, Astrabad) is contested, not owned, 1528-1530

keyframe_review.note: 767,162 km2 for 1526-1528: the 1521 land plus Herat, Merv, Mary, Andkhoy and Shibarghan. The Battle of Jam page has Ubaydullah 'eventually besieging Herat' in 1528, recapturing Astrabad and Mashhad, and losing at Jam in September 1528; Herat was surrendered later; the Merv page has the Safavids expel the Uzbeks from Merv in 1510 and the Uzbeks conquer it only in 1593. Neither page has an Uzbek Herat or Merv in 1526-1527. The owned land is the 1521 shape; Khorasan is a contested zone 1528-1530 (ledger).

384,306 km2 for 1529-1533: the 1521 land. The Battle of Jam page has the Uzbeks return to Khorasan after the battle and Herat surrendered 'in exchange for safe passage', then the Safavids 'managed to expel the Uzbeks again' by late 1530; the zone is in the ledger. Abu Said ruled Samarkand 1530-1533 and refused to help Ubaydullah (Ubaydullah page): the khanate was a group of appanages (the 1533 kurultai divided Bukhara, Samarkand, Tashkent and Balkh among the Abu'l-Khayrid lines, Khanate of Bukhara page).
384,828 km2 for 1534-1546: the 1521 land. Ubaydullah reigned 1534-1539; his move on Khwarazm (1538) ended in defeat; Power struggles among the Uzbeks lasted until 1556.

correction.text: the 1547 shape without Badakhshan, which Abdullah Khan II 'seized' in 1584

keyframe_review.note: 429,740 km2 for 1547-1587: the 1534 land plus 157 cells of Gorno-Badakhshan (Khorugh) that the shape holds from 1547, while the Abdullah Khan II page has the khan seize Badakhshan in 1584. Badakhshan is removed for 1547-1575 here; Tashkent (1576) and Badakhshan (1584) get their own new keyframes below. Samarkand, which Cliopatria draws inside the khanate throughout, joined his unified state by 1582 on the same page. No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the Bukharan land of 1547 without Badakhshan, with Tashkent and its oasis, taken in 1576

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1576-1583: He defeated armies from Samarkand and took Tashkent (1576) - Cliopatria's Bukhara row never holds Tashkent before 1598.

correction.text: the 1547 land with Badakhshan, plus Tashkent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1584-1587: Badakhshan was seized in 1584 and Tashkent held since 1576; Abdullah Khan II's son took and plundered Mashhad in 1583 (a raid).

union.text: Khorasan: the Iranian province with Mashhad, and Herat

correction.text: the 1588 land with Tashkent and Khorasan (1588: He seized Khorasan), 1588-1597; Merv added in 1593

keyframe_review.note: 430,409 km2 for 1588-1594: no Khorasan and no Tashkent. The Abdullah Khan II page has Khorasan seized in 1588 (a war with Iran from 1587 to 1598), Merv conquered in 1593 (Merv page), Khwarazm taken in 1593-94 (an occupation, ledger). The corrected shape holds for 1588-1597; Merv follows from 1593.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 1598-1599 only: the Kazakhs hold Samarkand and Fergana after Abdullah Khan II's death

keyframe_review.note: 337,211 km2: the 1588 land without Samarkand, Fergana, Andijan, Khujand and Jizzakh. Cliopatria starts it in 1595, three years before the event the Kazakh Khanate page dates: In 1598, the Kazakhs captured Tashkent, Turkistan, Andijan, and Samarkand, but failed to take Bukhara (Cliopatria's Kazakh row holds those towns from 1598 too). Shape unchanged, years 1598-1599.

337,211 km2 for 1600-1608: the same shape as 1595. The Balkh page says 'Balkh was ruled by Bukhara except for Safavid rule between 1598 and 1601', so the Balkh country is Safavid until 1601 (ledger); Merv went to the Safavids in 1600 (Merv page).

430,409 km2 for 1609-1635: Samarkand and Fergana back. No opened page dates the recovery; Cliopatria's Kazakh row drops Samarkand and Kokand by 1611, and the Kazakh page has Yesim fighting Baki Muhammad and Imam-Quli over Syr Darya cities. Recorded at confidence 1 in the ledger.
427,598 km2 for 1636-1686: nine Pamir cells fewer than 1609. The Balkh page has Shah Jahan turn Balkh into a Mughal subah in 1646 and lose it in 1647 (an occupation in the ledger).
427,457 km2 for 1687-1708: unchanged. Subhan Quli Khan 1680/81-1702 and Ubaidullah 1702-1711 reign (Janid page); no territory is given.

341,582 km2 for 1709-1720: the Fergana valley (Namangan, Fergana, Andijan, Osh, Kokand, Khujand) is gone. In 1709 Shahrukh Biy ... established the Koktonliq Ata fortress near Kokand, which began the khanate, 'the authority of the Khanate of Bukhara over the Fergana Valley was weakening'. Exact match with the shape change.

341,998 km2 for 1721-1737: unchanged. The Khanate page has the state disintegrate 'into multiple different principalities' after 1711 (Abu'l-Fayz's authority disputed), which Cliopatria does not draw. Balkh is lost in 1736 (ledger).

minus.text: the land south of the Amu Darya: Balkh and Kunduz, conquered by Nader Shah in 1736

correction.text: the 1738 shape without the Balkh country, taken by Nader Shah in 1736

keyframe_review.note: 341,582 km2 for 1738-1747: still holds Balkh and Kunduz south of the Amu Darya, which the Balkh page says Nader Shah conquered in 1736 (Cliopatria's Afsharid row never includes Balkh, and its Durrani row takes it in 1757). Nader conquered Khiva and made Bukhara submit in 1740 (Nader Shah page): a vassalage, no border (wars).

minus.text: the land south of the Amu Darya, which is not Bukharan after 1736

correction.text: the 1748 shape without the Balkh country

keyframe_review.note: 277,095 km2 for 1748-1751: 220 cells of the north-western desert (Zarafshon, Kyzylkum) are now Khiva's in Cliopatria's Khiva row; no opened page dates it, but after Nader's death in 1747 'the Uzbek khanates of Bukhara and Khiva regained independence'. Balkh as in 1738.

minus.text: the land south of the Amu Darya, which is not Bukharan after 1736

correction.text: the 1752 shape without the Balkh country

keyframe_review.note: 277,021 km2 for 1752-1756: Muhammad Rahim is ataliq 1747-1753 (Emirate page) and the khanate is a Manghit regency under Janid puppets. Balkh as in 1738.

266,125 km2 for 1757-1782: 93 cells south of the Amu Darya (Balkh, Kunduz, Mazar-i-Sharif) leave the shape and 51 Pamir cells come in; the south bank is already excluded by the corrected 1738 shape, so the visible change is the Pamir fringe. The Khanate page says Muhammad Rahim 'In 1754 he successfully incorporated Khujand, Tashkent, and Turkestan into the khanate'; this is not applied: the Kokand page has Khujand with Kokand until the 1860s and the Kazakh page has Tashkent Kazakh, and Cliopatria's shape holds none of the three. In November 1762 'Bukharan armies conquered the town of Charjuy and subdued the Turkmen' (Khanate page), a town the shape has held since 1516.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 1783-1785 only; from 1785 the Emirate of Bukhara

keyframe_review.note: 266,125 km2 for 1783-1787: unchanged. The Emirate page: 'officially created in 1785' when Shah Murad took the title of emir; the shape's years are shortened to 1783-1785 and the Emirate dossier takes 1785 onwards (Cliopatria's Emirate row starts 1788).

region.text: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1512: Babur is beaten at Ghazdewan and the Uzbeks keep Transoxiana. Ubaydullah defended Bukhara against Babur and the Safavids in 1511-1512 and the page says the victory 'finally secured the Uzbeks' possession of the land between Amu Darya and Syr Darya'. The Khanate of Bukhara page itself dates the khanate from 1501; here it opens where the Shaybanid row ends.

1512: Babur takes Samarkand. 'Samarqand was briefly lost to Babur in 1512' (the month and the Safavid backing are not on the page; the Balkh page has Babur ruling Balkh as a Safavid vassal in 1511-1512).
1512: Ghazdewan ends the contest for Samarkand; the Uzbeks recover it. The Cliopatria Timurid row (1512-1515, 3,241 cells over Transoxiana) outlasts it by three years.
1512: Bukhara recovers Balkh from Babur. The Balkh page has Babur rule it as a Safavid vassal in 1511-1512, but Bukhara defeated him twice and he retreated to Kabul (the page gives no month).

region.text: Tashkent, Turkestan, Sayram and the Syr Darya steppe held in Cliopatria's 1516 shape and not in its 1521 shape

ledger.note: Winter 1516-17: the Uzbeks march on Tashkent. 'In the winter of 1516-1517, Uzbek forces approached Tashkent but failed to capture it'; Kasym Khan had beaten a large Uzbek force in 1510.

About 1521: Kasym Khan's reign ends with the Syr Darya towns Kazakh. 'By the end of his reign, the southern borders of the Kazakh Khanate extended to the right bank of the Syr Darya, including Tashkent, Turkestan, and Sayram.'

region.text: Tashkent, Turkestan, Sayram and the Syr Darya steppe

ledger.note: About 1521: Tashkent, Turkestan and the Syr Darya steppe are Kazakh (see above); the year is Cliopatria's shape change and Kasym's reign end.
1528: Ubaydullah Khan 'recaptured Astarabad and Mashhad' and besieges Herat; Tahmasp relieves it and wins at Jam on 24 September 1528 ('Ultimately the Safavids emerged victorious').

Late 1530: the Safavids drive the Uzbeks out of Khorasan again. Tahmasp's revolt in Baghdad let the Uzbeks return, Herat 'was eventually surrendered in exchange for safe passage', and by late 1530 the Safavids 'managed to expel the Uzbeks again'. The year is the page's 'late 1530'; the Ubaydullah page lists five unsuccessful Khorasan offensives without dates.

region.text: Khwarazm, where Ubaydullah killed the local Khan Avanish

ledger.note: 1538: Ubaydullah Khan marches into Khwarazm, killing the local khan Avanish. The Khanate of Bukhara page says Khwarazm was 'briefly conquered by Ubaidullah Khan (1533-1539)'.
1538-39: Din Muhammad drives Ubaydullah out, and he dies in 1539 shortly after the Khwarazm defeat. The page does not date the expulsion.

ledger.counterpart: Shaybanid appanage of Samarkand and Tashkent
ledger.note: 1576: Abdullah Khan II takes Tashkent. He defeated armies from Samarkand and took Tashkent (the counterpart is the Samarkand-Tashkent Shaybanid appanage; the page names no ruler).
1584: Abdullah Khan II seizes Badakhshan (He seized Badakhshan). Cliopatria's shape holds it from 1547.

region.text: Khorasan: the Iranian province with Mashhad, and Herat

ledger.note: 1588: Khorasan is seized in the war with Iran that began in 1587 (He started a war with Iran in 1587 that lasted until 1598). The page names no towns for Khorasan; the Herat page is not among those opened.
1593: Abdullah Khan II conquers Merv.

1593-94: His troops conquered Khwarazm. He marched on Khiva, where the local sultans were captured and executed. The Khanate of Khiva page: 'Around 1540 and 1593, the Khans were driven out by the Bukharans.'
1598: Abdullah Khan II dies and the occupation of Khwarazm lapses. No opened page says when the Arabshahids returned (the Khiva page lists Arab Muhammad as khan 1602-1623); recorded at confidence 1.

region.text: Samarkand, the Fergana valley and Tashkent

ledger.note: 1598: Tauekel's Kazakhs overrun the east. In 1598, the Kazakhs captured Tashkent, Turkistan, Andijan, and Samarkand, but failed to take Bukhara; Abdullah Khan II's page: after his death the Kazakhs took Turkestan, Tashkent, Samarkand, and Andijan, but they withdrew from Bukhara.

region.text: Khorasan: the Iranian province with Mashhad, and Herat

ledger.note: 1598: the war with Iran ends in a Safavid recovery of Khorasan. The Abdullah Khan II page ends the war in 1598 and does not mention the loss; the Balkh page has Safavid rule at Balkh 1598-1601 and the Merv page has Shah Abbas take Merv by 1600.
1598: Balkh passes to the Safavids. 'Balkh was ruled by Bukhara except for Safavid rule between 1598 and 1601.'
1599: the Janid (Ashtarkhanid) dynasty replaces the Shaybanids. Baqi Muhammad Khan 'in 1599 defeated Pir Muhammad Khan II'; the khanate continues under the Janids to 1785.
1600: Merv goes to the Safavids. Safavid governor Biktash Khan Ustajlu was appointed after Shah Abbas took the city (1600).
1601: Balkh returns to Bukhara (Safavid rule 1598-1601).

region.text: Samarkand, Fergana and Khujand, back in the 1609 shape

ledger.note: 1609: Samarkand and Fergana are Bukharan again in Cliopatria's shape. No opened page dates it; the Janid page lists Baqi Muhammad, Vali Muhammad and Imam Quli with no territory; the Kazakh page has Yesim at Tashkent in 1611 and 1613 and fighting Baki Muhammad and Imam-Quli over Syr Darya cities.
1646: Shah Jahan takes Balkh. It was 'turned into a subah (imperial top-level province) in 1646 by Shah Jahan, only to be lost in 1647'.
1647: the Mughals lose Balkh again and Bukhara holds it.

region.text: the Fergana valley: Namangan, Fergana, Andijan, Osh, Kokand and Khujand

ledger.note: 1709: the Fergana valley breaks away. In 1709 Shahrukh Biy ... established the Koktonliq Ata fortress near Kokand, which began the khanate as 'the authority of the Khanate of Bukhara over the Fergana Valley was weakening'. The year is the page's; the region is the shape change.

1734: Ura-Tyube becomes the front with Kokand. Urateppe 'would be the focal point of almost constant fighting' with Bukhara for 140 years; earlier Abd al-Rahim Biy briefly seized Khujand, Ura-Tyube and the remnants of Samarkand (undated).

region.text: Balkh and Kunduz, the land south of the Amu Darya

ledger.note: 1736: Nader Shah conquers Balkh. 'In 1736 it was conquered by Nader Shah.' Cliopatria's shape keeps the Balkh country in the khanate until 1756. (Reviewer ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: region was the whole country of Afghanistan; now the khanate's 1721 shape south of the Amu Darya, the same land the 1738-1752 corrections remove.)

1747: the ataliq Muhammad Rahim kills Abu al-Fayz and his son, 'ending the Janid dynasty'; Manghit ataliqs rule behind Janid puppet khans until 1785. Nader Shah had died and 'the Uzbek khanates of Bukhara and Khiva regained independence' (Nader Shah page).

region.text: the desert fringe north-west of Bukhara

ledger.note: 1748: the north-western desert (Kyzylkum, Zarafshon) is Khiva's in Cliopatria's Khiva row. Nothing opened dates or names it; Khiva regained independence after Nader's death in 1747.
November 1762: 'Bukharan armies conquered the town of Charjuy and subdued the Turkmen.' Cliopatria's shape has held Charjuy since 1516; the event records the page, not a new cell.
1785: the khanate ends; the fighting over Ura-Tyube goes on into the Emirate period (for 140 years from 1734 on the Kokand page). The end year here is the dossier's, not the fighting's.
1785: Shah Murad becomes emir. The Emirate of Bukhara 'was officially created in 1785' when he 'formalized the family's dynastic rule' and took the title of emir instead of khan.

wars.name: Battle of Ghazdewan and the Babur-Uzbek war
wars.outcome: Babur takes Samarkand briefly and is beaten at Ghazdewan in 1512; the Uzbeks keep the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya.
wars.note: The Khanate page: 'Samarqand was briefly lost to Babur in 1512'. The Balkh page: Babur ruled Balkh as a Safavid vassal 1511-1512.

wars.name: Uzbek-Kazakh war over Tashkent and Turkestan

zones.text: Tashkent, Turkestan, Sayram and the Syr Darya steppe

wars.outcome: Kasym Khan holds the Syr Darya towns; the Uzbek advance on Tashkent in the winter of 1516-1517 fails.

wars.name: Battle of Jam and the Uzbek-Safavid war over Khorasan
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah recaptures Astarabad and Mashhad and besieges Herat; Tahmasp wins at Jam on 24 September 1528 with artillery; Herat is surrendered later and the Safavids expel the Uzbeks by late 1530.
wars.note: The Ubaydullah page dates a battle against Tahmasp on 24 September 1524 (a miniature caption) and speaks of five undated, unsuccessful Khorasan offensives; the Jam page's 1528 is followed.

wars.name: Ubaydullah Khan's Khwarazm campaign
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah kills Khan Avanish and is driven out by Din Muhammad; he dies in 1539.
wars.note: The Khanate page dates the conquest '1533-1539', the Ubaydullah page 1538.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's war with Safavid Iran

union.text: Khorasan: the Iranian province with Mashhad, and Herat

wars.outcome: Abdullah II seizes Khorasan (1588) and Merv (1593); the Safavids retake Balkh (1598-1601), Merv (1600) and Khorasan after his death.
wars.note: He started a war with Iran in 1587 that lasted until 1598; a non-aggression pact with Akbar freed him for it.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Khwarazm is occupied and the Khivan sultans executed; the Arabshahids return after 1598.

wars.name: Kazakh invasion of Transoxiana under Tauekel
wars.outcome: Tauekel takes Tashkent, Turkestan, Andijan and Samarkand in 1598 but fails to take Bukhara.

wars.name: Mughal occupation of Balkh
wars.outcome: Shah Jahan makes Balkh a Mughal subah in 1646 and loses it in 1647.
wars.note: No article on the war itself was opened; the Balkh page gives the two years.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Central Asian campaign
wars.outcome: Nader conquers Khiva and forces Bukhara to submit in 1740; Abu al-Fayz 'remained on the throne' as a vassal ('conquered by Persia', Janid page). The Balkh country goes to Nader in 1736. Bukhara and Khiva regain independence on his death in 1747.
wars.note: No border moves, so no zone; the afsharid-iran dossier should record vassal_start for khanate-of-bukhara in 1740 and vassal_end in 1747.

wars.name: Bukhara-Kokand wars over Ura-Tyube
wars.outcome: Constant fighting: Urateppe 'would be the focal point of almost constant fighting' with Bukhara for 140 years; Kokand keeps most of Khujand.
wars.note: The war continues into the Emirate (to 1874 by the page's count); the dossier of the Emirate should carry the zone on.

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers between a khanate of appanages, Kazakh and Turkmen nomads and Persia: no treaty line is drawn in this period. The Amu Darya is the only river-line frontier (against Nader Shah, 1740, and the Durrani later).

notes:
Khanate of Bukhara: 1512..1785 (Cliopatria 1516..1787, 19 shapes). Pages opened: 11 (KB, Ubaydullah Khan, Abdullah Khan II, Janid dynasty, Kazakh Khanate, Battle of Jam, Balkh, Merv, Khanate of Kokand, Emirate of Bukhara, Nader Shah), a little over the nine-page budget because Merv and Nader Shah are shared with the Khiva dossier.
Cliopatria problems and decisions:
- The state starts in Cliopatria at 1516; the Shaybanids row ends 1511; the Khanate page dates the khanate from 1501. Split here at 1511/1512 (new keyframe khanate-of-bukhara_1512 for 1512-1515; the Timurid row 1512-1515 covers Transoxiana in the same years, which is Babur's brief hold and should end 1512: for the ia-02 reviewer).
- 1516-1520: Tashkent, Turkestan and the Syr Darya steppe removed (Kazakh Khanate page); contest zone 1516-1521.
- 1526-1528: Herat/Merv are not supported by the Jam or Merv pages; made a contest zone 1528-1530.
- 1547: Badakhshan from 1547 against the page's 1584; Tashkent absent although taken in 1576; both added by new keyframes 1576 and 1584; Khorasan/Tashkent 1588-1597 by an adjusted 1588.
- 1595: begins 1598 on the Kazakh page.
- 1738-1756: Balkh and Kunduz removed from 1736 (Balkh page: conquered by Nader Shah in 1736; independent under Haji Khan in 1747). Cliopatria's Afsharid row never holds Balkh and its Durrani row takes it from 1757: who held Balkh 1736-1756 and when the Durrani took it needs the Durrani or Balkh article (not opened: page budget).
- 1783-1787: ends 1785 (Emirate created 1785); the Emirate dossier should start in 1785 (Cliopatria 1788).
Disagreements between pages: Abdullah II's accession (1557/1561/1581/1583); Janid end (1747 / 1756 / 1785); Muhammad Rahim ataliq from 1745, 1747 or 1753 (Khanate page) vs 1747 (Emirate page); the capital date 1562 vs Abdullah's reign; Ubaydullah's Khwarazm conquest (1533-1539 vs 1538, and 'conquered' vs a defeat); Jam (24 September 1528) vs the 'Sarikamish 24 September 1524' caption on the Ubaydullah page; the Khanate page's claim that Muhammad Rahim 'incorporated Khujand, Tashkent, and Turkestan' in 1754, contradicted by the Kokand and Kazakh pages and not applied.
Not settled: the 1709-1747 decay ('multiple different principalities', 1711); Fergana's recovery 1609 (page silent); the north-western desert to Khiva 1748 (page silent). Vassalage under Nader Shah (1740-1747) is not an event type for the vassal: the afsharid-iran dossier (me-10) should carry vassal_start/vassal_end for this state. The Khanate page has a future-dated citation (24 June 2026) and a footnote claim 'from Kashgar to the Aral Sea' that nothing else supports; ignored.
Shape areas could not be compared with an infobox figure: the Khanate page gives no area (only an estimated 1902 population).
